sources.excerpt: Published on September 19, 2015 Cultco overdrive pedal Information Cultco As heard on almost every track of Joywave's "How Do You Feel Now?", this pedal shines on guitar, bass, and synth. A collaboration with Adventure Audio, the unit ranges from a subtle "always on" overdrive to a ratty, metallic distortion. The single EQ knob allows for a wider range than traditional guitar pedal "tone" knobs. A 9V power supply is required but not included. Hand crafted in Rochester, NY. Specifications: 9V center negative power supply Power consumption: (around) ~25mA Weight: ~ 1 lb Dimensions: 4.77" x 2.6" x 1.39" Blue LED IMPORTANT NOTE: The Cultco 001 does not include a power supply. Must provide your own 9V power supply (something like a Visual Sound 1 SPOT or similar). Cultco 001 Medium Overdrive - Pedal of the Day
sources.excerpt: Posted By Pedal of the Day on Tuesday, September 29, 2015 in Adventure Pedals, Cultco, Overdrive / Distortion | 0 comments I had never come across a pedal that had been produced initially for one specific band, much less one that had been used on almost every track of a major label album release, with little or no exposure or advertising. That is until I was contacted by the band Joywave about featuring an overdrive pedal they had created with Adventure Audio , to which I was instantly intrigued, and decided that I had better check it out. A few days later, the 001 Medium Overdrive from Cultco arrived on my doorstep, and the adventure had begun. The 001 Medium Overdrive is just that, but can get a little nasty if you need it to as well. Boasting an easy-to-use control knob section, it appears to be an ordinary overdrive, but therein lies the deception. Featuring a nice Gain range and an even bigger EQ range, this slick pedal will do just about any drive tone you can think of, and while not exactly a wall of distortion when cranked, it’s not trying to do something it can’t. With the Gain turned down, you still get a nice, mellow growl, one that you can just leave on all the time if you want, to add some beef to your tone. Crank it up a bit, and you’ve got a warm and meaty overdrive, with a boatload of sustain that will make any amp sing. Plus, when you play around a bit with the Equalizer control knob, you can get some great low-end presence, as well as a sharp and clear but not offensive treble tone, perfect from ripping solos and cutting through mixes with ease. I dig the clean, simplistic graphic design of this overdrive, and the simple control layout suits me just fine as well. Plus, it’s not often I get to work directly with a band who had a single go to #1 on the Billboard Alternative charts (“Dangerous”, check out the awesome video HERE ), which is pretty rad in my book. Thanks to Joywave and Cultco for bringing this incredibly under-the-radar overdrive to my attention, hope we can get more people to check it out as well!
